title: Search for Majorana Bound States in Short Chains of Proxmitised Quantum Dots
authors: Bogdan R. Bułka, Karol I. Wysokiński
abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZM) appearing at the ends of artificially created one-dimensional p-wave superconductors have been intensively studied recently both theoretically and experimentally. Among possible platforms, proximitised semiconducting wires, and short chains of quantum dots with a superconductor in between were investigated. Here, we propose a different platform consisting of a chain of quantum dots (QDs) sandwiched between an s-wave superconductor and a strong spin-orbit semiconductor, subject to a Zeeman magnetic field. Neglecting spin-conserving hopping processes between QDs and local on-dot superconducting correlations induced by the superconducting proximity effect, reduces the Hamiltonian to the sum of two equivalent Hamiltonians with two independent Hilbert spaces. The resulting model has a staggered structure due to spin-flipping processes $t_{so}$ and cross-Andreev reflections $Δ_{CAR}$ between neighbouring dots. Our central result is the phase diagram of a short chain consisting of four QDs and coupled to two external reservoirs, obtained by means of the Green function in chiral Majorana representation. The modulus of the retarded Green function, probing the whole chain and calculated for zero energy, is shown to contain information on topology and spatial character of Majorana zero modes. The features observed in the Green function nicely agree with those obtained from the transfer matrix approach. In particular the region in parameter space in which Majorana zero modes display oscillatory wave functions are well reproduced. Likewise the borders of the fermion parity changes obtained by the Green function agree with those obtained by other means.
summary: This work theoretically explores the existence and nature of Majorana Zero Modes in a quantum dot chain coupled to superconductors. By employing multiple advanced methods—including Green functions and transfer matrices—the authors map out the phase diagram, confirming the topological protection of these zero-energy states. The findings provide a detailed guide for engineering superconducting quantum devices hosting exotic topological excitations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the search for Majorana Zero Modes (MZM) in a specific artificial platform: a short chain of quantum dots (QDs) coupled to superconductors and semiconductors.
main_result: The analysis confirms that the system exhibits distinct topological regimes, characterized by the appearance of zero-energy modes, which are consistently predicted by multiple theoretical approaches (Green function, transfer matrix).
method: The study employs advanced theoretical techniques including the Green function formalism in chiral Majorana representation, the transfer matrix method, and the calculation of topological invariants (Pfaffians).
model_or_system: The system is a chain of QDs sandwiched between an s-wave superconductor and a strong spin-orbit semiconductor, subjected to a Zeeman field. The model is analyzed via an effective Hamiltonian derived under several approximations.
key_observables:
The modulus of the retarded Green function at zero energy, the energy spectrum ($\omega_{0,nQD}$), and the topological invariant ($
u$).
important_parameters: Chemical potential ($\mu$), Zeeman field ($V_z$), and the coupling strengths ($t_{so}$, $\Delta_{CAR}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis neglects spin-conserving hopping processes and local on-dot superconducting correlations, and often assumes a large superconducting gap limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum for varying QD lengths (2QD, 4QD, 6QD) and show phase diagrams mapping out topological boundaries based on $\mu$ and $V_z$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian, calculates the spectrum using the Green function and transfer matrix approaches, and then compares the resulting phase diagrams and signatures (oscillatory vs. localized wavefunctions) derived from these complementary methods.
why_interesting: The rigorous comparison between Green function and transfer matrix results provides a robust theoretical confirmation of topological phase transitions in mesoscopic superconducting structures, which is highly relevant for designing superconducting quantum circuits.
